children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures remained on the upswing late Thursday morning.
An analyst said canola was benefiting from another round of hikes in crude oil. The latter was on the rise as the Middle East situation became more tense.
The spillover from crude had yet to erase losses in other vegetable oils, although the Chicago soy complex and European rapeseed were attempting to turn positive. Malaysian palm oil remained mixed.

Wide range in temperatures: Over the next couple of days Prairie temperatures are to range from the mid-teens to the mid-20s Celsius, with Saskatchewan being the warmest. Rain is expected for parts of southern Manitoba as well as central Alberta while Saskatchewan is to remain dry through the weekend.

Harvest progress: Co-operative weather will help with the region's harvest, which largely remains slow. Saskatchewan is set to release its weekly crop report today. Manitoba said its canola harvest was 43 per cent complete as of Sept. 21.
Technicals: The November canola contract climbed further above its 20-day moving average after closing slightly ahead of it on Wednesday.
Canola crush margins halted their contraction, expanding by a small amount. The November positions were 269.77 Canadian dollars to C$276.94 per ton above the futures.
Loonie: The Canadian dollar continued its backslide late Thursday morning as the United States dollar gained strength. The loonie fell to 70.68 U.S. cents, compared with Wednesday's close of 70.94.
Contracts: Approximately 33,850 canola contracts were traded as of 11:35 a.m. EDT with prices in Canadian dollars per metric ton:
